messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm kicking a staging deploy in ~20m for the config flag tweak on ranking. Not changing model or API contract. Thoughts on versioning? patch bump or keep v1.4.2 and annotate?

deploy-bot: Release queued: build 781a2f4 · tests: unit ✅ integ ✅ smoke pending · target=staging · eta=20m

mira: If it's visible behavior change to end users (ranking order) we should bump the patch. Even small regressions are easier to track with a new patch.

sam: Agree. Patch makes rollback semantics simpler for clients using pinned deps. Also our release tooling expects unique tags per deploy.

jen: Quick counter: this is an internal config toggle behind a feature flag, no public API change. Can we use build metadata instead? e.g. `v1.4.2+cfg.2021` so semver precedence stays same.

mira: build metadata doesn't show up in all places and our deploy routing/rule engine strips it. Not reliable for user-facing pinning.

alex: My worry: patch proliferation — we had 5 tiny patches last sprint. Ops prefers fewer patch bumps unless behavior changes. But ranking change -> behavior change.

sam: proposal: bump patch to v1.4.3, tag with release notes that clearly mark "internal flag: ranking experiment" and mark rollout as canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

jen: +1 on rollout. Also put a line in release notes: `chore(ranking): enable config flag behind ff; no API change; canary rollout` so it's searchable.

alex: ok. tagging command then: 
```
git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "v1.4.3 chore(ranking): enable internal config flag (canary)"
git push origin v1.4.3
```

mira: For rollback criteria, let's be explicit: "If 5xx rate increases >1% absolute or latency p95 regresses >200ms across canary slice for 5m, rollback to v1.4.2". Ops next?

sam: I'll add an automated rule to the deploy pipeline: if errors>1% for 5m -> rollback and notify #incidents. Also enable immediate manual rollback if paging.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v1.4.3 -> staging slice 5% · canary monitors active · uid=deploy-981

jen: Small docs note: add a line to release-notes.md under unreleased: `- v1.4.3: chore: enable ranking config flag (canary). Rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Rollback if errors or latency spike.`

alex: done, pushed note. Also adding tag to changelog entry: `# Changelog
## 1.4.3 (2026-03-20)
- chore(ranking): enable internal config flag (canary) — alex`

mira: Final question for future: should we add a short internal guideline: "if change affects user-visible ordering/behavior, prefer patch bump even if behind flag" — to reduce bikeshedding.

sam: yes. I'll draft a 2-line policy and put it in RELEASE_GUIDELINES.md: `Behavioral changes (including ranking, sorting, defaults) = patch bump; pure telemetry/observability config = no bump unless rollout changes semantics.`

alex: sweet. rolling canary now. will monitor dashboards. ping me if you see anything odd. :thumbsup:
